title: How to Use an ATS to Hire Your First 10 Employees (November 2026)
summary: Learn how to use an ATS to hire your first 10 employees as a startup in November 2026. Get structured hiring processes that reduce mis-hires and save time.
body_markdown:
When you[hire your first 10 employees](https://www.dover.com/) , every decision sets the foundation for what follows. A mis-hire at this stage can cost months of momentum and real money. An applicant tracking system gives early-stage teams a way to manage that process without losing candidates in spreadsheets or missing follow-ups. This guide breaks down how to use an ATS to run a structured hiring process from your first role through your tenth.


**TLDR:**


- An ATS keeps early hiring organized while founders juggle recruiting with other work.
- Structured scorecards and pipelines reduce mis-hires, which can cost up to 30% of first-year salary.
- A fractional recruiting partner can handle sourcing and coordination at startup scale.
- Getting your first 10 hires right sets repeatable patterns for the next 50.
- Free ATS tools and startup-friendly pricing let you run a structured process without burning runway.


## Why Startups Use an ATS to Hire Their First 10 Employees


Most startups pick up an ATS earlier than they expect to. The first few hires usually start in a founder’s inbox and a shared spreadsheet, which works fine until two or three roles open at once and candidates start slipping through the cracks. Setting up a simple ATS before that point takes little time and saves a lot of cleanup later.


There is also a candidate experience side to it. Strong early candidates are usually talking to several startups at once, and a slow reply or a lost resume tells them a lot about how the company runs. An ATS sends confirmations, keeps every conversation in one record, and flags when someone has sat in a stage too long. It also gives you a record to learn from later, showing where your best candidates came from and which questions told you the most.


For most startups, the appeal comes down to a few practical realities:


- Founders juggle recruiting with everything else, so one place to track applicants, schedule interviews, and collect feedback keeps the process from falling apart.
- Early hiring often involves multiple stakeholders, and an ATS creates a shared record instead of competing versions of a conversation.
- An ATS helps you apply the same process to every candidate, reducing the risk of overlooking someone good or advancing someone for the wrong reasons.


## What to Look for in an ATS before You Hire Your First 10 Employees


Not every ATS fits early-stage startups, and the wrong pick can slow you down. An[ATS can provide measurable benefits](https://www.uschamber.com/co/run/human-resources/smbs-applicant-tracking-software-benefits) for small teams, but only when the features match your stage.


### Features That Actually Matter at the Early Stage


Look for these before signing up for anything:


- [Job posting distribution](https://www.dover.com/blog/first-5-hires-seed-stage-startups) that pushes roles to multiple job boards automatically.
- A candidate pipeline view showing where every applicant stands at a glance.
- Interview scheduling that syncs with your calendar to cut back-and-forth.
- Collaboration tools letting a co-founder or hiring manager leave feedback directly.
- Reporting on time-to-fill and source quality to show what’s working.


### Pricing That Fits a Startup Budget


Many ATS tools charge per seat or per job posting, which adds up fast. Look for free tiers or startup-friendly pricing that won’t punish you for hiring in bursts. Flat monthly pricing tends to be more predictable when headcount grows unevenly.

## How to Hire Your First 10 Employees Using Your ATS


Each stage of early hiring maps to a specific ATS workflow.


### Requisition and Job Posting


Start by creating a job requisition inside your ATS. Define the role, hiring manager, and approval chain before the job goes live. Many ATS tools publish directly to multiple job boards from one interface, saving time when posting across LinkedIn, Indeed, and niche boards.


### Building Your Pipeline


Set up a custom pipeline for each role with stages like Applied, Phone Screen, Technical Interview, Offer, and Hired. As candidates move through stages, your ATS tracks touchpoints so fewer details fall through.


### Structured Scorecards


Attach a scorecard to each stage so every interviewer[rates candidates against the same criteria](https://hbr.org/2024/06/choosing-between-a-structured-or-conversational-interview) , keeping decisions grounded in data instead of gut feeling.


### Offer and Onboarding Handoff


Once a candidate clears the final interview, generate the offer inside the ATS and connect it to your HRIS if integrations are available. Keeping this handoff in one system reduces errors and helps new hires get up to speed faster.


## How Hiring Your First 10 Employees Fits Into Your Full Hiring Pipeline


Your first 10 hires set patterns for[your next 50 hires](https://www.dover.com/blog/scale-10-to-50-employees-without-recruiter) . When candidates move through a structured pipeline inside an ATS, from job boards and referrals through scorecards to onboarding, those patterns stay repeatable; when parts happen in inboxes and spreadsheets, you inherit the chaos instead.


Here’s what typically goes wrong without one:


- Candidate data disappears, so you can’t re-engage strong candidates later.
- Evaluation gets inconsistent without shared scoring criteria.
- Without analytics, you can’t tell which sources are working.


Early hires often come through personal networks. Tracking referrals from day one gives you visibility into your[most reliable hiring channel](https://erinapp.com/blog/employee-referral-statistics-you-need-to-know-for-2025-a-game-changer-for-enterprise-recruitment/) before scaling.


## When to Bring in a Fractional Recruiter to Support Hiring Your First 10 Employees


Hiring your first 10 employees pulls founders in every direction at once. You’re closing deals, managing product, and trying to run a hiring process that actually works. At some point, the recruiting work starts to crowd out everything else, and that’s often when bringing in outside help makes sense.


An ATS gives you the system of record: pipeline, scorecards, scheduling. A[fractional recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-a-fractional-recruiter-guide) adds capacity on top, handling sourcing, outreach, and screening inside the same ATS, so the founder still sees every candidate in one place. A founder filling one or two generalist roles can often run the process alone with an ATS. Parallel openings, senior roles, or specialized technical positions are usually where a recruiter earns its keep.


### Signs It’s Time to Get Help


- You have[multiple open roles at once](https://www.dover.com/blog/signs-startup-hire-recruiter) with no clear system for tracking candidates.
- Roles stay open longer than planned because sourcing keeps getting pushed aside.
- You’re making offers without a consistent interview process, risking legal exposure and inconsistent hires.


The cleanest setup is one where the recruiter and hiring team share one ATS, so handoffs and candidate history live in one place. Dover’s[fractional recruiting](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-costs) lets startups choose experienced recruiters from a marketplace, and those recruiters can work directly inside its free ATS, or in an existing tool like Ashby, Greenhouse, or Lever.


## The Cost of Getting Your First 10 Hires Wrong as a Startup


A bad early hire costs more than most founders expect. Some hiring estimates suggest a bad hire can cost[up to 30%](https://www.apollotechnical.com/cost-of-a-bad-hire/) of that employee’s first-year earnings. For a $120,000 role, that’s $36,000 gone before you’ve seen any return, plus slower teams, management headaches, and stalled momentum at a stage when none of that is affordable.


### Why Early Hiring Mistakes Are Hard to Reverse


On a small team, every person carries disproportionate weight, so a weak engineer, an unfocused sales rep, or a disorganized ops hire affects everyone around them.


- Misaligned hires often need weeks of management time before a founder accepts the fit is wrong.
- Replacing someone mid-stage means re-opening a search while the remaining team absorbs extra work.
- Culture patterns set early tend to compound, making poor decisions harder to undo as the company grows.

## FAQs


### Can I build a structured hiring process without bringing on a full-time recruiter?


Yes. An ATS gives you the tools to run a repeatable hiring process without needing a dedicated recruiter on staff. Most early-stage teams use an ATS to manage pipelines, scorecards, and interview coordination while founders or hiring managers own the final decisions.


### What’s the difference between using an ATS and hiring a fractional recruiter?


An ATS is software that organizes candidates, stages, scorecards, and scheduling, while a fractional recruiter is a person who sources, reaches out to, and screens candidates on your behalf. Many founders can typically handle one or two open roles on their own with just an ATS. A recruiter tends to become worth the cost once several roles are open at the same time, a role is senior or specialized, or sourcing keeps getting pushed aside for other work. The two often work best together when the recruiter operates inside the same ATS, so the hiring team can keep visibility into the full pipeline.


### What features actually matter in an ATS before you hit 10 employees?


Look for job board distribution, a clear candidate pipeline view, interview scheduling that syncs with your calendar, and collaboration tools that let your team leave feedback without separate threads. Early on, simplicity beats feature depth: you need something that works immediately instead of requiring weeks of configuration.


## Final Thoughts on Using an ATS to Hire Your First 10 Employees


The way you[hire your first 10 employees](https://www.dover.com/) shapes every decision that follows, and the right tools make that process repeatable instead of chaotic. Dover’s free ATS paired with fractional recruiters is one example of what structured early hiring can look like, without the overhead of enterprise software or agency fees. What fits your team comes down to how many roles are open at once, weighed against how much of a founder’s week recruiting is already consuming.
